bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban reduced the primary efficacy end point versus placebo (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96).
implications: These data support that, versus placebo, rivaroxaban was associated with a lower Kaplan–Meier rate of the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96), while being associated with higher rates of TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs. 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%) and no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66); the document also reports that the 2.5-mg twice-daily dose reduced cardiovascular and all-cause mortality whereas the 5-mg twice-daily dose did not significantly reduce those mortality outcomes.

major_points.text: Trial design: double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial with two rivaroxaban doses.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 15,526 patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome to receive twice-daily doses of either 2.5 mg or 5 mg of rivaroxaban or placebo

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point definition: composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy result: rivaroxaban reduced the primary composite end point vs placebo.
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban significantly reduced the primary efficacy end point, as compared with placebo, with respective rates of 8.9% and 10.7% (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96; P = 0.008)

major_points.text: Safety: rivaroxaban increased major bleeding not related to CABG and intracranial hemorrhage vs placebo, without a significant increase in fatal bleeding.
major_points.quote: rivaroxaban increased the rates of major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.009), without a significant increase in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66)

major_points.text: 2.5 mg twice daily dose showed reduced cardiovascular death and all-cause death vs placebo (a survival benefit not seen with 5 mg twice daily).
major_points.quote: The twice-daily 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxaban reduced the rates of death from cardiovascular causes (2.7% vs. 4.1%, P = 0.002) and from any cause (2.9% vs. 4.5%, P = 0.002), a survival benefit that was not seen with the twice-daily 5-mg dose.

major_points.text: Population characteristics: index event mix included STEMI, NSTEMI, and unstable angina; median time from index event to randomization 4.7 days.
major_points.quote: The index event was a STEMI in 50.3% of the patients, an NSTEMI in 25.6%, and unstable angina in 24.0%. The median time from the index event to randomization was 4.7 days (interquartile range, 3.2 to 6.0).

absolute_effects.text: Primary efficacy end point rates: 8.9% with rivaroxaban vs 10.7% with placebo.
TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG: 2.1% with rivaroxaban vs 0.6% with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote: major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001)

absolute_effects.text: Intracranial hemorrhage: 0.6% with rivaroxaban vs 0.2% with placebo.
Number needed to treat statement: 1 prevented per 56 treated for 2 years.
absolute_effects.quote: the composite end point would be prevented in 1 patient if 56 patients were treated for 2 years with rivaroxaban.

subgroups.text: Results were examined according to major subgroups with interaction testing performed.
subgroups.quote: Results were examined according to major subgroups for general consistency of treat- ment effect, and interaction testing was per- formed.

subgroups.text: Primary efficacy end point reduction was consistent among subgroups except for patients with a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack.
subgroups.quote: The reduction in the primary efficacy end point with rivaroxaban was consistent among the subgroups except for patients with a history of stroke or transient is­ chemic attack

harms.text: Fatal bleeding did not differ significantly between combined rivaroxaban and placebo (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).
harms.quote: There was no significant difference in the rates of fatal bleed- ing associated with rivaroxaban as compared with placebo (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).

harms.text: Rates of adverse events not related to bleeding were similar in rivaroxaban and placebo groups.
harms.quote: The rates of adverse events that were not re- lated to bleeding were similar in the rivaroxaban and placebo groups

harms.text: Premature discontinuation of treatment occurred in 26.9% (2.5 mg), 29.4% (5 mg), and 26.4% (placebo).
harms.quote: premature discontinuation of treatment occurred in 26.9% of patients receiving the 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxa- ban, 29.4% receiving the 5-mg dose of rivaroxaban, and 26.4% receiving placebo.

analysis_methods.text: Efficacy analyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach with prespecified censoring rules tied to treatment phase and discontinuation.
analysis_methods.quote: efficacy analyses were performed with the use of a modified intention-to-treat ap- proach, which included the randomized patients and the end-point events that occurred after ran- domization and no later than the completion of the treatment phase of the study

analysis_methods.text: Power based on 983 primary efficacy events to detect a 22.5% relative reduction with two-sided type I error rate 0.05.
analysis_methods.quote: We determined that a total of 983 primary efficacy end-point events would provide a power of approximately 96% to detect a 22.5% relative reduction

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios and two-sided 95% confidence intervals were used; rates expressed as Kaplan–Meier estimates through 24 months.
analysis_methods.quote: We used hazard ratios and two-sided 95% con- fidence intervals to compare the study groups. Rates of the end points were expressed as Kaplan– Meier estimates through 24 months.

analysis_methods.text: Primary safety analysis included all randomized patients who received at least one dose of study drug, evaluated from first dose until 2 days after discontinuation.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary safety analysis included all patients who underwent randomiza- tion and who received at least one dose of a study drug, with evaluation performed from the time of administration of the first dose of a study drug un- til 2 days after the discontinuation of a study drug.
